questions.stem: In an experiment aimed at understanding DNA replication, a piece of radio-labeled DNA is allowed to undergo two rounds of replication within a non-radioactive medium. This setup is designed to track the distribution of the original radioactive material across the generations of DNA. Based on the known mechanism of semiconservative replication, what would be the expected outcome regarding the radioactivity of the DNA strands after two replication cycles?

options.label: A
options.text: All the strands will have radioactivity

options.label: C
options.text: Half of the DNA will have no radioactivity

options.label: D
options.text: Three–fourth of the DNA replicated will have radioactivity

questions.answerText: Half of the DNA will have no radioactivity
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Half of the DNA will have no radioactivity

questions.stem: When considering the process of mRNA maturation in eukaryotic cells, a critical step involves the removal of certain sequences before the mRNA can be translated into a protein. There's a statement that needs verification: "Introns are excised by RNA editing." Is this statement accurate regarding the process by which introns are removed from pre-mRNA?

options.label: A
options.text: TRUE, as RNA editing is the mechanism that ensures introns are removed from pre-mRNA.

options.label: B
options.text: TRUE, because RNA editing and intron removal are synonymous terms in molecular biology.

options.label: C
options.text: FALSE, intron removal is accomplished through splicing, not RNA editing.

options.label: D
options.text: FALSE, RNA editing is primarily involved in modifying exon sequences and doesn't excise introns.

questions.answerText: FALSE, intron removal is accomplished through splicing, not RNA editing.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) FALSE, intron removal is accomplished through splicing, not RNA editing.

questions.stem: Restriction fragment length polymorphism analysis can only be used to follow the inheritance of a genetic disease if:

options.label: A
options.text: mRNA probe is used in combination with antibodies

options.label: B
options.text: The disease-causing mutation is at or closely linked to restriction site

options.label: C
options.text: Mutation is outside of restriction sites so that cleaving still occurs

options.label: D
options.text: Restriction fragments remain the same size but their charge changes

questions.answerText: The disease-causing mutation is at or closely linked to restriction site
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) The disease-causing mutation is at or closely linked to  restriction site

questions.stem: A 3.5-year-old girl of Arabian descent presents to the clinic with severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, leukocytosis, and elevated ESR. The history provided by her parents includes fever, cough, pallor, weakness, and tachypnea. On examination, hepatomegaly is noted. Following diagnostic evaluations, sickle cell anemia (SCA) is diagnosed. Based on the information provided, which of the following statements about SCA is false?

options.label: A
options.text: RFLP result from a single base change

options.label: B
options.text: Single nucleotide change results in change of Glutamate to Valine

options.label: C
options.text: HbS confers resistance against malaria in heterozygotes

options.label: D
options.text: ‘Sticky patch’ is generated as a result of replacement of a nonpolar residue with a polar residue in Sickle Cell Anemia (HbS)

questions.answerText: ‘Sticky patch’ is generated as a result of replacement of a nonpolar residue with a polar residue in Sickle Cell Anemia (HbS)
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) ‘Sticky patch’ is generated as a result of replacement of a nonpolar residue with a polar residue in Sickle Cell Anemia (HbS)

questions.stemHtml: A genetic counsellor is reviewing the case of 7-month-old boy diagnosed with Tay-Sachs disease, an autosomal recessive disorder. If son is a diagnosed case of Tay-Sachs disease, the family's pedigree and Southern blot analysis with RFLP linked to the Tay-Sachs gene have been presented to determine the genetic status of their daughter. What does the Southern blot analysis indicate regarding the daughter's genetic status concerning Tay-Sachs disease?

options.label: A
options.text: She has 25% chance of having Tay-Sachs disease.

options.label: B
options.text: She has 50% chance of having Tay-Sachs disease.

options.label: C
options.text: She is a carrier for Tay-Sachs disease.

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) She is homozygous normal.
